root_cause.text: The tilcdc_fini() function unconditionally calls drm_kms_helper_poll_fini() and drm_atomic_helper_shutdown() without checking whether the DRM device was successfully registered, causing these cleanup functions to be invoked on partially-initialized state during probe failure/deferral.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description and commit message explicitly state that these helpers "should only be called when the device has been successfully registered" and that they are "called unconditionally in tilcdc_fini(), which causes warnings during probe deferral scenarios." The kernel backtrace shows drm_atomic_helper_shutdown being called from tilcdc_fini when invoked from the probe error path (tilcdc_pdev_probe). The patch fixes this by restructuring the error handling in tilcdc_init() so that tilcdc_fini() is only called after full registration, and by adding specific cleanup labels that avoid these functions for earlier failures.

candidates.rationale: Unconditionally called during probe failure even if device not registered; poll helper may be uninitialized, causing NULL deref or use-after-free.
Unconditionally called during probe failure on potentially uninitialized atomic state, leading to crashes or memory corruption.
Invoked from init_failed path after probe failure; triggers the unconditional cleanup calls in tilcdc_fini on partially initialized device.
If this registration fails, control flows to init_failed and tilcdc_fini; the device state is incomplete, yet the subsequent cleanup lacks proper guards.
The is_registered flag is only set after successful registration; cleanup functions in tilcdc_fini ignore this flag, leading to calls on unregistered devices.
Contrast with unconditional calls: this check guards crtc_shutdown, highlighting the missing guards for drm_kms_helper_poll_fini and drm_atomic_helper_shutdown.

vuln_statements.explanation: This unconditional call during probe failure or deferral invokes poll helper cleanup on a device that may not have been fully registered, leading to NULL dereference or use-after-free.
This unconditional call on a partially initialized device (before successful drm_dev_register) can cause crashes or memory corruption due to uninitialized atomic state.
Called from the init_failed error path after probe failure; it triggers the unconditional cleanup functions in tilcdc_fini without checking registration status, thereby causing the vulnerability.

If this registration fails, control flows to init_failed and tilcdc_fini, but the device state is incomplete. The subsequent cleanup lacks proper guards, making this a critical control flow point for the vulnerability.

This flag is set only after successful registration, yet tilcdc_fini ignores it. Missing a check of this flag before calling drm_kms_helper_poll_fini and drm_atomic_helper_shutdown is the direct root cause.

In contrast to the unconditional calls, this guard correctly protects drm_crtc_force_disable_all. Its presence highlights the inconsistency and missing guards for the other cleanup functions, making it relevant to the vulnerability analysis.

bic_trace_step.reason: In tilcdc_unload() (lines 86-117), the functions drm_kms_helper_poll_fini(), drm_mode_config_cleanup(), and drm_vblank_cleanup() are called unconditionally. In tilcdc_load(), the fail label goto path calls tilcdc_unload() regardless of which initialization steps succeeded. For example, if modeset_init() fails (line 252), drm_vblank_init() has not been called yet, but drm_vblank_cleanup() will still be executed in tilcdc_unload. Similarly, drm_kms_helper_poll_init() is called only at line 274, but drm_kms_helper_poll_fini() is called in tilcdc_unload even if an earlier error occurred. This matches the root cause: cleanup functions invoked on partially-initialized state during probe failure/deferral. No conditional checks exist to prevent this, so the vulnerable construct is present and not fixed.
